evidence.significance: AWAIT BOUNDARY after tryClaimToken() claims the token. Yields control while holding atomic claim—between line 71 (tryClaimToken succeeds) and line 84 (new token inserted). Window where other requests can interleave.

evidence.quote: UPDATE refresh_tokens SET revoked_at = ? WHERE id = ? AND revoked_at IS NULL
evidence.significance: Atomic conditional UPDATE. Exactly one of two concurrent requests wins (changes=1). Loser gets 0 rows—correctly throws InvalidToken without calling revokeFamily().
Losing concurrent request throws InvalidToken immediately. Does NOT call revokeFamily(). This is the current correct behaviour.

Grace window (5s) prevents revokeFamily() when a token is found already-revoked within 5 seconds. This is the key guard that distinguishes concurrent race (grace) from real stale-token theft (outside grace).
revokeFamily() sweeps ALL tokens in the family, including any newly inserted winner token. This is why calling revokeFamily() incorrectly (e.g. without grace window) destroys the winner's new token.
